propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model ID contains a colon, causing canonical Bedrock versioned IDs (e.g. us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0) to lose their provider prefix

The naive colon-presence test (if ':' in model) cannot distinguish between a provider separator and a colon within a Bedrock model's version suffix, causing the two code paths (_resolve_target and infer_provider) to independently mis-parse the input

An explicitly configured provider must be checked first and never overridden by punctuation or inference from the model string; conflicting provider specifications should raise LLMConfigError rather than silently choosing one
The qualified/unqualified decision must be centralized in one helper function (split_provider_qualifier) so both _resolve_target and infer_provider use the same logic and cannot drift apart
